summary: An import record with no nodes. The definitions and theorems that the six layers of this roadmap name are declarations of EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons (stages EC.0–EC.5), a roadmap with the same title, the same parent and the same source route, whose 100-node plan an independent review has accepted; the one exception, Chen's isogeny theorem, is an input the owner records as a gap. To plan them here would plan them twice, so this packet plans nothing: targetCoverage gives, for each of the 31 targets, the imported declarations, baseline consequences and recorded gap routes; imports lists the declarations that were read; restructure proposes merging this roadmap into its owner. Nothing is formalised and no layer is mathematically closed: the owner's layers are planned, with their own gaps and requests.

targetCoverage.target: Kraus's rationality threshold F
targetCoverage.statement: For N ≥ 1, with μ(N) = [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] and g⁺(N) the complex dimension of the weight-two newspace of Γ₀(N) with trivial character, F(N) = (√(μ(N)/6) + 1)^(2g⁺(N)), a real number.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same definition on the same carriers: the native index, and the trivial-character part of the Γ₁(N) newspace. The owner's API (krausF_eq, one_le_krausF, krausF_of_dimension_zero) and its tests at levels 1, 11 and 35 cover what the threshold is used for; 3 + 2√2 = (√2 + 1)².

targetCoverage.target: Kraus's two-torsion threshold G
targetCoverage.statement: For N ≥ 1, G(N) = (√(μ(lcm(N, 4))/6) + 1)², a real number; the level is lcm(N, 4), not 4N and not the radical of N.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same definition. The owner tests levels 1, 4 and 11, and 13 + 4√3 = (√12 + 1)². The value G(2) = 4 and the invariance of G under lcm(N, 4) = lcm(M, 4) follow from its formula krausG_eq.

targetCoverage.target: Kraus's comparison threshold H
targetCoverage.statement: For N ≥ 1, H(N) = max(F(N), G(N)).
targetCoverage.comparison: The same definition, with krausF_le_krausH, krausG_le_krausH and krausH_lt_iff. That F cannot replace H is visible at level 11: F(11) = 3 + 2√2 < 13 + 4√3 = H(11), the owner's tests krausF_eleven and krausH_eleven.

targetCoverage.target: Martin's sharp weight-two newspace bound
targetCoverage.statement: For every N ≥ 1, 12·g⁺(N) ≤ N + 1, with equality exactly when N = 35 or N is a prime congruent to 11 modulo 12.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement with the same equality cases. The owner also plans the proof: Martin's prime-power table, the identification of his arithmetic expression with the actual newspace dimension, and the estimates and finite checks of his §4 (EC.0/local-factors to EC.0/bounded-family).

sources.locator: Theorem 2, p. 3; §4, Lemmas 16–22 and its proof, pp. 14–16 (v1)

targetCoverage.target: The norm bound behind a congruence
targetCoverage.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d, λ a prime of its ring of integers above the rational prime ℓ, and x a nonzero element of λ whose image under every embedding K → ℂ has absolute value at most B. Then ℓ ≤ |Norm_{K/ℚ}(x)| ≤ B^d.
targetCoverage.comparison: The lower bound ℓ ≤ |Norm(x)| is EC.1/prime-divides-integral-norm, with the Mathlib declarations on ideal norms it rests on. The owner states the upper bound for the two elements to which it is applied, p + 1 ∓ c_p (EC.1/trace-norm) and b − a_q(f) (EC.3/bounded-integer-trace-norm). The general inequality |Norm(x)| ≤ B^d is the product formula over embeddings in Mathlib and is not a target of its own. Precisely, mathlib:Algebra.norm_eq_prod_embeddings gives the product, and mathlib:AlgHom.card gives exactly d complex embeddings. Taking absolute values and multiplying the d bounds gives B^d. Nonzero x and an embedding force B > 0; no extra assumption B ≥ 1 is used. This is a consequence of these baseline declarations and the imported lower bound, not a separately owned theorem.

sources.locator: §2, proof of Lemma 2.2, p. 359; general consequence of the cited Mathlib product formula

targetCoverage.target: The removed-prime exponent bound
targetCoverage.statement: Let E/ℚ have conductor M and minimal discriminant Δ, let ℓ ≥ 3 be a prime with E[ℓ] irreducible, and let M₀ be M divided by the primes q with q ∥ M and ℓ | ord_q(Δ). If p ≠ ℓ is a prime with p ∥ M and ℓ | ord_p(Δ), then ℓ ≤ (√p + 1)^((M₀+1)/6).
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement and hypotheses (Bennett–Siksek, Lemma 2.2), with M₀ the deletion level of SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6 and ord the valuation exponent. The owner splits the proof into the nonvanishing of p + 1 ∓ c_p, the bound by the degree of the coefficient field, the bound of that degree by g⁺(M₀), and the comparison of real powers.

sources.locator: §2, Lemmas 2.1–2.2 and proof, p. 359

targetCoverage.target: Rationality from finitely many prime coefficients
targetCoverage.statement: If a normalized newform f of weight two, level N and trivial character has c_q ∈ ℤ for every prime q ≤ μ(N)/6, then every Fourier coefficient of f is in ℤ.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement (Kraus, Lemme 1), with the additional conclusion that the coefficient field is ℚ.

sources.locator: §3.2, Lemma 1 and proof, pp. 1144–1145

targetCoverage.target: Integrality of the small prime coefficients above F(N)
targetCoverage.statement: Let ℓ ≥ 5 be prime, E/ℚ with E[ℓ] irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, and f a normalized newform of weight two, level N and trivial character whose residual representation at a prime above ℓ is E[ℓ]. If ℓ > F(N), then c_q ∈ ℤ for every prime q ≤ μ(N)/6.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner states the stronger conclusion that the coefficient field of f is ℚ, with the same contradiction with ℓ > F(N): a non-integral coefficient at a prime q ≤ μ(N)/6 with q ∤ N differs from an integer trace, or from ±(q + 1), by a nonzero element of the prime above ℓ whose norm is at most F(N). The existence of f is EC.3/exact-weight-two-lift.

sources.locator: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3, p. 1145

targetCoverage.target: The elliptic curve of a rational newform
targetCoverage.statement: A normalized newform f of weight two, exact level N and trivial character with integer coefficients has an elliptic curve F/ℚ of conductor exactly N with a_q(F) = c_q at the primes of good reduction; if ℓ ≥ 5 is prime and the residual representation of f at a prime above ℓ is an irreducible E[ℓ], then F[ℓ] ≅ E[ℓ] as representations of the absolute Galois group of ℚ.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement, from the one-dimensional quotient of J₀(N) (ModularCurvesPartII R14.5) and the conductor theorem (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4).

sources.locator: §3.1, rational-coefficient paragraph before equation (7), p. 1143

targetCoverage.target: Kraus's rational comparison theorem
targetCoverage.statement: For E/ℚ and a prime ℓ ≥ 5 with E[ℓ] irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, if ℓ > F(N) there is an elliptic curve F/ℚ of conductor exactly N with F[ℓ] ≅ E[ℓ].
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement (Kraus, Théorème 3); the modularity of E that Kraus assumes is EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/modularity-theorem.

sources.locator: §3.1, Theorem 3, p. 1144

targetCoverage.target: Finite recognition of point counts modulo four
targetCoverage.statement: For a (modular) elliptic curve C/ℚ of conductor N, 4 divides #C(𝔽_q) for every prime q ∤ 2N as soon as it does so for every such prime q ≤ μ(lcm(N, 4))/6.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner states the contrapositive: a failure of the divisibility at some prime q ∤ 2N occurs at such a prime below the bound (Kraus, Appendice II, Corollaire). It also plans what the proof rests on: Kraus's congruence criterion modulo a power of a prime, his local filters, and the comparison with the Eisenstein series Σ_{n odd} σ₁(n)qⁿ on Γ₀(4).

sources.locator: Appendix II (§8), Proposition 2 and Corollary, pp. 1158–1159

targetCoverage.target: Transfer of the point counts to the comparison curve
targetCoverage.statement: Let ℓ ≥ 5 be prime, E/ℚ with full rational 2-torsion and E[ℓ] irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, and C/ℚ of conductor exactly N with C[ℓ] ≅ E[ℓ]. If ℓ > G(N), then 4 divides #C(𝔽_q) for the primes q ∤ 2N.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner's lemma has this conclusion, for every prime q ∤ 2N, and argues by contradiction from a small prime at which the divisibility fails. Kraus's argument passes through two intermediate facts at the primes q ≤ μ(lcm(N, 4))/6, good reduction of E and the equality a_q(E) = a_q(C); the owner does not state them as conclusions.

sources.locator: §3.3, equations (10)–(11) and trace comparison, p. 1146

targetCoverage.target: Repair of rational two-torsion by a two-isogeny
targetCoverage.statement: If C/ℚ has 4 | #C(𝔽_q) at every odd prime of good reduction, there is an isogeny C → F over ℚ of degree 1 or 2 onto a curve with full rational 2-torsion; it preserves the conductor and, for odd ℓ, the representation on ℓ-torsion.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner plans three nodes: the existence of the rational point of order two, the square-class dichotomy on the model y² = x(x² + ax + b), and the selection of a curve with full two-torsion by an isogeny of degree at most two. The transport of the conductor and of the ℓ-torsion along that isogeny is the last step of EC.3/kraus-full-two-realization. The owner's hypothesis is at every odd prime of good reduction, which is what the application provides; Kraus allows finitely many exceptional primes, and that form is not planned.

sources.locator: §3.3, final two-isogeny paragraph, p. 1146

targetCoverage.target: Kraus's full two-torsion realization
targetCoverage.statement: If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion, ℓ ≥ 5 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, and ℓ > H(N), then there is an elliptic curve F/ℚ of conductor exactly N with full rational 2-torsion and F[ℓ] ≅ E[ℓ].
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement (Kraus, Théorème 4). Bennett and Siksek quote it, as their Theorem 4, at the level M₀ of their Theorem 3; the passage from M₀ to N(E[ℓ]) is the next target.

targetCoverage.target: From the deletion level to the residual conductor
targetCoverage.statement: Kraus's theorems are stated at the prime-to-ℓ conductor N(E[ℓ]) and Serre weight 2; an application at the deletion level M₀ needs N(E[ℓ]) = M₀ and weight 2 as separate facts.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner states N(E[ℓ]) = M₀ for ℓ ≥ 5 when E has good reduction at ℓ, or multiplicative reduction at ℓ with ℓ | ord_ℓ(Δ) (EC.3/deletion-level-exact-adapter); the case ℓ ∤ M is its good-reduction case. It rests on the comparison of conductor exponents away from ℓ (EC.3/deletion-conductor-away), whose full local form the owner requests from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3. For ℓ ≥ 11 the owner attributes to Kraus the deduction of the reduction alternative from Serre weight 2 and requests that local theorem; for ℓ = 5, 7 it keeps the alternative as a hypothesis.

sources.locator: §2, Theorems 3–4, pp. 359–360; application adapter with separate local-conductor and weight hypotheses

targetCoverage.target: Mazur's theorem on isogenies of prime degree
targetCoverage.statement: If E/ℚ has a rational cyclic isogeny of prime degree r, then r ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 37, 43, 67, 163}; if moreover E has no complex multiplication over an algebraic closure, then r ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 37}.
targetCoverage.comparison: The list of twelve primes is EC.4/mazur-prime-isogeny-classification, with Mazur's argument planned in the nodes it cites (the Eisenstein quotient, the formal immersion, the isogeny character and its three cases). The list of eight primes for curves without complex multiplication is EC.5/large-prime-isogeny-cm.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, pp. 129–130; introduction table and CM discussion, p. 129; §7, Theorem 7.1, pp. 153–155

targetCoverage.target: No cyclic isogenies of degree 2ℓ or 4ℓ
targetCoverage.statement: No elliptic curve over ℚ has a rational cyclic isogeny of degree 2ℓ for a prime ℓ ≥ 11, or of degree 4ℓ for a prime ℓ ≥ 7.
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner plans the whole list of degrees of rational cyclic isogenies, {1, …, 19, 21, 25, 27, 37, 43, 67, 163}. It contains no even number above 18, hence no 2ℓ with ℓ ≥ 11 and no 4ℓ with ℓ ≥ 5.

sources.locator: §3, irreducibility applications in Lemmas 3.3 and 3.5, pp. 361–363; the composite-degree exclusions are imported from the owner’s separate Mazur–Kenku node

targetCoverage.target: From two-torsion and an invariant line to a cyclic isogeny
targetCoverage.statement: Let ℓ be an odd prime and E/ℚ have a Galois-stable subgroup of order ℓ. If E has a rational point of order 2, it has a rational cyclic isogeny of degree 2ℓ; if E has full rational 2-torsion, a curve isogenous to E over ℚ has a rational cyclic isogeny of degree 4ℓ.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same three arguments: the sum of the coprime kernels; the cyclic kernel of order 4 of the composite E/T → E → E/T′ for distinct rational subgroups T, T′ of order 2; and the sum of that kernel with the transported line.

sources.locator: §3, Lemmas 3.3 and 3.5, pp. 361–363; derived coprime-kernel and dual-isogeny argument, not a separately stated source lemma

targetCoverage.target: Irreducibility with full rational two-torsion
targetCoverage.statement: If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion and ℓ ≥ 7 is prime, then E[ℓ] is irreducible, and absolutely irreducible.
targetCoverage.comparison: Irreducibility is the owner's theorem (Bennett–Siksek, proof of Lemma 3.3). Absolute irreducibility follows from the cited node of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4, because E[ℓ] is odd.

sources.locator: §3, Lemma 3.3 proof, p. 362; absolute irreducibility uses the separately imported oddness lemma

targetCoverage.target: Irreducibility with a rational point of order two
targetCoverage.statement: If E/ℚ has a rational point of order 2 and ℓ ≥ 11 is prime, then E[ℓ] is irreducible, and absolutely irreducible.
targetCoverage.comparison: Irreducibility is the owner's theorem (Bennett–Siksek, proof of Lemma 3.5); absolute irreducibility follows as in the preceding target.

sources.locator: §3, Lemma 3.5 proof, p. 363; absolute irreducibility uses the separately imported oddness lemma

targetCoverage.target: Potential good reduction under a nonsplit Cartan image
targetCoverage.statement: If p ≥ 5 is prime and the image of the Galois representation on E[p] lies in the normalizer of a nonsplit Cartan subgroup, then E has potentially good reduction at p and at every prime q ≢ ±1 mod p.
targetCoverage.comparison: The same statement (Lemos, Proposition 2.2) in contrapositive form: a prime of potentially multiplicative reduction is different from p and congruent to ±1 modulo p.

sources.locator: §2, Proposition 2.2 and proof, pp. 4–5 (v2)

targetCoverage.target: The Cartan correspondence and Chen's isogeny
targetCoverage.statement: For r ∈ {2, 3, 5, 7, 13} and a prime p outside that set, the correspondence through X₀(r) ×_{X(1)} X(p)/(N_sp ∩ N_ns) maps the Jacobian of X₀(rp²)/w_{p²} to the Jacobian of X₀(r) ×_{X(1)} X_ns⁺(p), commutes with the Hecke operators T_n for n prime to p, and vanishes on the p-old part. (Chen's theorem, that the induced map on the p-new quotient is an isogeny, is an input the owner records and does not plan as a node.)
targetCoverage.comparison: The owner plans the homomorphism, its Hecke equivariance and its vanishing on the p-old part (Lemos, Lemma 3.2), with the quotient by w_{p²} that keeps the level structure at r. That the induced map is an isogeny (Chen; Lemos, Theorem 3.3), and its use in EC.5/finite-winding-quotient, are in the owner's gap “Chen isogeny and higher-dimensional winding quotient” and in its proposal of a continuation of ModularCurvesPartII for Cartan correspondences. The case r = 1, which no target uses, is not planned.

restructure.detail: These two roadmaps are one roadmap planned twice. Both extend EllipticCurveModularity, both have the title “Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons”, and both plan the Part II route of the Bennett–Siksek extraction that continues EllipticCurveModularity (research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20.result.json, items 08, 09, 10, 57, 59, 60 and 82), which names EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons as its roadmap. The packet of EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons has 100 nodes over its stages EC.0–EC.5, was accepted by independent-review-REV-DESIGN-EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons on 2026-10-06 and is live in the atlas; ErdosProgressionPowers, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations and the document of EllipticCurveModularity cite it. The first version of this packet restated 31 of its declarations under new identifiers. Each of them is matched with its owner in targetCoverage. One statement of the first version is a declaration of neither roadmap: Chen's theorem that the Cartan correspondence is an isogeny on the p-new quotient. The owner uses it, records it in a gap and assigns it to a continuation of ModularCurvesPartII; the first version also left it as a gap awaiting a shared owner. Where the two plans differed in substance, the owner is the more careful: it keeps the reduction alternative at ℓ = 5, 7 in the passage from the deletion level to the residual conductor, and it records as a mistake of the source the claim in Lemos's preprint that the Jacobian of X₀(37) has rank zero. In several places the first version stated more than the owner does: the formal immersion and the two integrality statements for every prime p outside {2, 3, 5, 7, 13} where the owner has p > 37; Chen's isogeny, as above; finitely many exceptional primes in the repair of two-torsion; the norm inequality for a general element; and invariance of surjectivity under twist at p = 3. The exported theorems use none of these wider forms; they are described in targetCoverage and notesForOwner. Of the other continuations of EllipticCurveModularity, modularity over imaginary quadratic fields and abelian varieties of GL₂-type have roadmaps of their own, and the wild 3-adic route has a design job of its own (research/blueprint/splits.json), so no direction is left for the identifier EllipticCurveModularityPartII. Its stage ids are cited outside its own files only by EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic, which lists the stage EC.6 as a user of two of its nodes (IQ.2/symplectic-twist and IQ.4/cartan-curves), in its packet and in the matching lines of its document. The roadmap id is also named in that packet's proposal on Cartan compactifications, in research/blueprint/focus.json and in research/blueprint/splits.json.
restructure.proposal: Keep one roadmap. Recommended: EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons stays the single owner of the effective residual comparisons, with its stages EC.0–EC.5 and its node identifiers unchanged, and EllipticCurveModularityPartII is retired: its definition, packet, document and suggested file leave the atlas, and its stages map to the owner's as EC.1 → EC.0 and EC.2; EC.2 → EC.1 and EC.3; EC.3 and EC.4 → EC.3; EC.5 → EC.4 and EC.5 (the non-CM prime-isogeny restriction); the absolute-irreducibility consequences also retain ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4; EC.6 → EC.5. The mentions of EllipticCurveModularityPartII:EC.6 in EllipticCurveModularityImaginaryQuadratic become EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5, and the owner takes this roadmap's place among the parties of that packet's proposal on Cartan compactifications. In research/blueprint/splits.json, EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons joins the directions split off from the combined Part II design of EllipticCurveModularity, so that the Bennett–Siksek route is designed by the job that has planned it and no combined design remains. If the identifier EllipticCurveModularityPartII is preferred for the surviving roadmap, the owner's files and identifiers are renamed to it instead. In either case the surviving plan is the owner's packet, and this packet contributes no declaration to it.

notesForOwner.note: With full rational two-torsion, E[ℓ] is irreducible already for ℓ = 5: a reducible E[5] would give, by EC.4/full-two-times-prime, a rational cyclic isogeny of degree 20 on an isogenous curve, and 20 is not in the list of EC.4/mazur-kenku-cyclic-degrees. The range ℓ ≥ 7 is the one the route asks for. At ℓ = 3 the statement fails: y² = x(x + 5)(x + 32) has three distinct rational roots and P = (4, 36). The tangent slope is 7 and 2P = (4, −36) = −P, so P has order three. This is an explicit counterexample, without invoking a torsion-classification supplier.

The owner's nodes EC.5/cartan-cusp-formal-immersion and EC.5/cartan-denominator-exclusion are stated for p > 37, while Lemos's Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 2.1 are stated for every prime p outside {2, 3, 5, 7, 13}. The conditions on the residue characteristic that their proofs use (q > r, q > 3, good reduction of the quotient at q, and ramification index 1 < q − 1) hold in the whole of that range: a prime q ≡ ±1 mod p with p ≥ 11 is at least 2p − 1 ≥ 21, since p ± 1 is even. So the restriction to p > 37 is not forced by small residue characteristics, and the inputs recorded in the owner's gap on Chen's isogeny and the winding quotient are stated by Lemos for the same wider range.

A proof of the selection lemma EC.3/four-count-full-two-selection that uses only the action on E[4]. Suppose every g in the image G of Galois in GL₂(ℤ/4) has det(1 − g) ≡ 0 mod 4, which Chebotarev's theorem gives from the point counts, and that the image modulo 2 has order 2, fixing the point P = 2e₁ for a basis e₁, e₂ of E[4]. Write g(e₁) = a·e₁ + c·e₂ and g(e₂) = b·e₁ + d·e₂; then a, d are odd, c is even, and det(1 − g) ≡ −bc mod 4, so c ≡ 0 mod 4 or b is even. An element t of G that is nontrivial modulo 2 has b odd, hence c ≡ 0. If some h in G had c ≡ 2, then h would be trivial modulo 2 and th would have b odd and c ≡ 2d ≡ 2, a contradiction. So every element of G maps e₁ to ±e₁, and G acts trivially on {Q in E[4] : 2Q ∈ ⟨P⟩}/⟨P⟩, which is the two-torsion of E/⟨P⟩. This avoids the Weierstrass model and the halving criterion of EC.3/four-count-square-classes. The statement about subgroups of GL₂(ℤ/4) is proved in this roadmap's suggested file.

A locator. In arXiv:1702.01985v2 the statement that the correspondence kills the p-old part is Lemma 3.2 (p. 9), quoted from Darmon–Merel, Lemma 6.2(a); the owner's node and its source finding E2 call it Proposition 3.2. Theorem 3.1 there is Chen's theorem and Theorem 3.3 the isogeny for r in {1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 13}.

The weight-two Eisenstein combinations E₂(z) − t·E₂(tz) with t > 1, from which the series Σ_{n odd} σ₁(n)qⁿ on Γ₀(4) is built (t = 2 and t = 4), are specified in the upstream layer tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-0-diamond-operators-and-modular-forms-with-character-nebentypus, in its treatment of Eisenstein series with character at the exceptional weight 2. The owner's node cites Layer 10 and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2 and has no request for the series; Layer 0 is the layer whose stated scope covers its construction.
